area.key: On this overview, a selection of the most important recommendations is compiled for your convenience. Improve your visitors' experience by solving these issues
Over here you can see all current recommendations. By default, recommendations are ordered by their importance. Use the inputs and dropdowns to filter and sort the recommendations.

This tab shows the redirects that are configured for your website. The various controls on this page allow you to create, delete and edit your redirects. This page only shows standard redirects. Check out the 'advanced redirects' tab to see all the redirects.
In addition to the standard redirects, this page shows you all redirects with advanced configuration options.

This entry indicates that an image could not be found. As a consequence, certain pages may not be displayed correctly and visitors might lack visual context to the content on particular pages. Check out the referrer information to see on which pages the image is requested. Redirect this url to an existing image to restore the user experience. Alternatively, you can check out the referrer overview below to see from which pages the image is requested. After manually repairing the images, this recommendation will eventually disappear.

This entry indicates that a file could not be found. As a consequence, certain pages may contain broken links to downloadable content. Visitors may not be able to download the files on those pages. Check the referrer information to see on which pages the downloadable content is referenced. Repair the downloads on those pages and this recommendation will eventually disappear. Alternatively, you can create a redirect to redirect all urls to a new file at once.
This entry indicates that a page could not be found. This means that visitors are trying to visit pages that don't exist. Create a redirect to redirect users to a new content page.

This entry indicates that a technical file could not be found. The consequences of this depend on the nature of the file. You should contact your administrator to get instructions on what to do with this. If you really know what you're doing, you may create a redirect for this file, but you likely shouldn't.

A permanent redirect is better for your site’s performance, but cannot be changed afterwards. Permanent redirects are a signal to google and other search engines to update their search results to the target that you specify. It makes the internet “forget” your incoming URLs so to speak.
Enter the URL which should be redirected from
Select where the URL should redirect to
Enabling this feature will apply this redirect on the incoming URL, even if content exists on the incoming URL.

A temporary redirect will redirect users to a different page, but will also tell google and other search engines that the content on this URL will be back later. Use this option if content is only temporarily moved to a different URL.
You run a campaign but it’s momentarily suspended and will be continued next month or year

A permanent redirect will redirect users to a different page, but will also tell google and other search engines that the current URL is no longer relevant. Use this option if content is moved to a different URL forever.
You used to post your blogs on /news, but they are now found below /blogs
You rely on an image in a social media post, but the image no longer exists or has moved
Sometimes a url might pop up in here that you simply cannot do anything with. In that case, you can ignore the recommendation and it will be permanently removed from the overview.
